min_weight_matching gives incorrect results
<!-- If you have a general question about NetworkX, please use the discussions tab to create a new discussion -->

<!--- Provide a general summary of the issue in the Title above -->

Consider the following graph:
```python
G = nx.Graph()
G.add_edge(1, 4, weight=2)
G.add_edge(2, 3, weight=2)
G.add_edge(1, 2, weight=1)
G.add_edge(3, 4, weight=4)
nx.min_weight_matching(G)
```

### Current Behavior
<!--- Tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior -->
The program returns `{(2, 1), (4, 3)}`
### Expected Behavior
<!--- Tell us what should happen -->
There are two maximal matchings in the graph, (1,2)(3,4) with weight 1+4=5, and (1,4)(2,3) with weight 2+2=4. The minimum weight maximal matching should be (1,4)(2,3) which has weight 4.
### Steps to Reproduce
<!--- Provide a minimal example that reproduces the bug -->
Run the code provided
### Environment
<!--- Please provide details about your local environment -->
Python version: 3.9
NetworkX version: 2.7.1


### Additional context
<!--- Add any other context about the problem here, screenshots, etc. -->
From the documentation and the code, `min_weight_matching` is simply taking the reciprocal of the weights and uses `max_weight_matching`. This logic seems to be faulty in this example: 1/1+1/4>1/2+1/2.

Integers are not normalized
## The Curse of the Floating BPM Value

### Problem

Beets currently allows the Model to set and the library to store any value for a field which is declared as `types.INTEGER` in the Item class. This behaviour however is not supported by MediaFile and for fields (such as bpm) which are [declared as integers](https://github.com/beetbox/mediafile/blob/master/mediafile.py#L1735)  these values are casted to integer before being written to the audio file tags. This results in the Model remaining always dirty and hence in the impossibility to have the library fully aligned with the media files.

This issue has been reported in #762 and discussed [here](https://discourse.beets.io/t/beet-write-bpm-quirk/738) on the forum. I am opening a new issue because even though this issue is most evident with the bpm field in reality it affects all fields declared `types.INTEGER` [in the Item class](https://github.com/beetbox/beets/blob/master/beets/library.py#L437).

In short, for any item in the library which has a bpm value in a non-integer format:
```text
     ...
     bpm: 119.434509277
     ...
```

Running this command:
```sh
$ beet write
```

will produce:

```
...
Madness - Full House: The Very Best of Madness - My Girl
  bpm: 119 -> 119.434509277
...
```

repeatedly. The audio file, if inspected through `beet info "My Girl"` will report:
```text
    ...
    bpm: 119
    ...
```
Therefore library and mediafile will remain forever out of sync.

### Setup

* OS: macOS 10.13.6
* Python version: 3.7.6
* beets version:  1.4.9 ([master](https://github.com/beetbox/beets/commit/8b8d223755662f499125b913ec9298faf3a2e3b2))

ParserError's should not return 500 HTTP status codes
When the Lark parser is unable to parse a filter in an unhandled way, we throw a `ParserError`, which inherits directly from `Exception` and thus the server treats it as a 500 Server Error.

Instead this should raise a 400 Bad Request and return the Lark error message.

This is something that has been biting OPTIMADE implementations that use k8s, as 500 is treated as "down endpoint" status code (cc @shyamd).

Handling of DS too long to be encoded in explicit encoding
<!-- Instructions For Filing a Bug: https://github.com/pydicom/pydicom/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#filing-bugs -->

#### Description
This is probably not a bug, but I'm not sure about the wanted behavior.
An RTPlan dataset encoded as Little Endian Implicit contains multiple values in the DS tag DHV Data (3004,0058) with an overall length not fitting into 2 bytes. Trying to write this as explicit Little Endian fails with an exception (`"ushort format requires 0 <= number <= (0x7fff * 2 + 1)"`) which is raised by the `pack` call in `write_leUS` while trying to write the length.

The standard says for this case in PS3.5, Table 6.2-1 (for VR DS):
```
Note
Data Elements with multiple values using this VR may not be properly encoded if Explicit-VR transfer syntax is used and the VL of this attribute exceeds 65534 bytes.
```
So, as I understand it, this is valid DICOM, that cannot be converted to explicit encoding without data loss.
The question is how to handle this. What comes to mind:
- truncate the value and log a warning
- raise a meaningful exception
- adapt the behavior depending on some config setting

WPS503 on for ... else with except in loop
### What's wrong

wps reports a useless else clause after a for, but I don't think the clause is useless

```
"""Test WPS503."""


def action_one(key: int) -> int:
    """
    Do some complicated logic for group of keys.

    Condition key % 2 != 0 and key < 10 is just example

    :param key: input_value
    :return: action result
    :raises ValueError: if key not in allowed list
    """
    if key % 2 != 0 and key < 10:
        raise ValueError()
    return key * 2


def action_two(key: int) -> int:
    """
    Do some complicated logic for group of keys.

    Condition key % 3 != 0 and key > 10 is just example

    :param key: input_value
    :return: action result
    :raises ValueError: if key not in allowed list
    """
    if key % 3 != 0 and key > 10:
        raise ValueError()
    return key * 3


# we have many actions
actions = [action_one, action_two]

input_value = 1

# We need to loop over actions, and stop after any action that can be applied.
# If not actions can be applied we raise ValueError
for action in actions:
    try:
        output_value = action(input_value)
    except ValueError:
        continue
    break
else:
    raise ValueError()

```

Redundant `boundary` if files/data is empty
If you try to send a post request with empty data and files — you will create a body with one `--boundary--` string, which can break the server.

It's because httpx create MultipartStream for `data={}, files={}`:
https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/a82adcc933345c6b8cb1623b031eb85723e7665b/httpx/_content_streams.py#L332-L334

And this MultipartStream doesn't have special behavior for empty data/files:
https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/a82adcc933345c6b8cb1623b031eb85723e7665b/httpx/_content_streams.py#L277-L283

Reproducible example:

```
from httpx.content_streams import encode

stream = encode(data={}, files={}, boundary=b"+++")
print(b"".join([part for part in stream]))
# b'--+++--\r\n'
```

I see two ways to solve it:
1. Check files not only for None but also for emptiness in `_content_streams.decode`
2. Check the count of fields in `MultipartStream.__init__` and doesn't write anything if fields are empty.

I already opened PR (#861) with a test example. If someone tells me which of these options is better, I will be happy to implement it  🙌

Infinite recursion on _STIXBase object deserialization
Hi!

There seems to be a bug in the way the `__getitem__`/`__getattr__` functions are implemented in `_STIXBase` (_cti-python-stix2/stix2/base.py_). The bug can be reproduced by trying to serialize/deserialize an object instance, resulting in infinite recursion causing the program to terminate with a `RecursionError` once the max recursion depth is exceeded. 

Here is a short example with copy.copy() triggering the recursion:
```
import copy, stix2
indicator = stix2.Indicator(name="a", labels=["a"], pattern="[file:name = 'a']")
copy.copy(indicator)
```

I believe this is because the unpickling tries to find the optional `__set_state__` method in `_STIXBase`. But since it's not there, the `__getattr__` is being called for it. However, the way `__getattr__` is implemented in the class, the `__getitem__` is called which  tries to look up an item in `self._inner`. Due to the way the deserialization works in general, the object itself is empty and the `__init__` was never called - meaning that the `_inner` attribute was never set. The access attempt on the non-existent `_inner` however triggers a call to `__getattr__` again, resulting in the recursion.

Here are two possible patches, I'm not sure though if that's the proper way of fixing it:

1) Checking for `_inner` access in `__getitem__`:
```
def __getitem__(self, key):
    if key == '_inner':
        raise KeyError
    return self._inner[key]

```
2) Checking for protected attributes in `__getattr__`:
```
def __getattr__(self, name):
    if name.startswith('_'):
        raise AttributeError(name)
    if name in self:
        return self.__getitem__(name)
    raise AttributeError("'%s' object has no attribute '%s'" %
                         (self.__class__.__name__, name))
```

Thanks!

```python
class BaseSpider(Spider):

        @returns requests 1
        """
        return Request('http://scrapy.org', callback=self.returns_item)

```

```
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 0 contracts in 0.000s
```

Using separate user agent for robots.txt
The current implementation of `RobotsTxtMiddleware` ([link](https://github.com/scrapy/scrapy/blob/master/scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/robotstxt.py)) uses `USER_AGENT` setting and `User-Agent` header of the request to determine the user agent to use for matching in `robots.txt`. There is no easy way for a user to send one user-agent header value but have a different user agent string evaluated to decide which pages to crawl. This use case seems to be more common that we thought previously for example - while [Googlebot](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/182072?hl=en) uses `"Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1; +http://www.google.com/bot.html)"`  as `User-Agent` header of the request, it actually uses user agent `"Googlebot"` in `robots.txt` for deciding which pages to crawl. [Here is the an article describing this.](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/1061943?hl=en) The same seems to be the case with Bing - [link](https://www.bing.com/webmaster/help/which-crawlers-does-bing-use-8c184ec0). Infact, Google made this distinction very clear in their proposed [robots.txt specification](https://github.com/google/robotstxt/blob/master/protocol-draft/draft-rep-wg-topic-00.txt) where they described the user agent used in `robots.txt` as the "product token".

The proposed solutions are implementing a new `ROBOTSTXT_USER_AGENT` setting, implementing a `robotstxt_user_agent` meta key for overriding user agent per request or both. Here is a thread that has previous discussion on the topic - https://github.com/scrapy/scrapy/pull/3796#discussion_r300036852.

I'm creating this issue as a place for discussion regarding whether to add this functionality into Scrapy? If yes, which route we should take?

The Use of `stream_output=False` is not Respected within a Controlled Console
### Describe the bug

For `subprocess.run()`, `stream_output=False` is not respected when the console is controlled. This is most likely to happen when a Wait Bar is started and a nested subprocess call uses `stream_output=False`.

I noticed this when building an APK without the Android emulator available. The `Building...` Wait Bar is started for the APK build and the emulator is now checked for and [installed](https://github.com/beeware/briefcase/blob/main/src/briefcase/platforms/android/gradle.py#L125) in-line. Because the `sdkmanager` script uses a progress bar, this installation [uses](https://github.com/beeware/briefcase/blob/main/src/briefcase/integrations/android_sdk.py#L439) `stream_output=False`....but it is in fact streamed.

### Steps to reproduce

```
briefcase build android && rm -rf ~/.cache/briefcase/tools/android_sdk/emulator && briefcase build android -v
```
